disclaimer: Informational, not legal advice. Verify with the legislation, the Energy Networks Association and your own Distribution Network Operator before relying on any value here.

northern_ireland.note: Northern Ireland is deliberately out of scope for the DNO section. It does not appear in the Energy Networks Association distribution licence area table, and regulation 3 of SI 2026/848 does not extend to Northern Ireland. Regulations 1 and 2 of that instrument do.

legislation.title: The Plugs and Sockets etc. (Safety) Regulations 1994 and Electricity Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations 2002 (Amendment) Regulations 2026
legislation.signed_by: Martin McCluskey, Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State, Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

extent.note: The extent is not uniform. Regulation 3, which amends the Electricity Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations 2002, does not extend to Northern Ireland.

legislation.what_it_permits: Regulation 2 allows a notified body to approve a type of standard plug for use with a plug-in microgenerator even though it does not conform to BS 1363, where the only non-conformity is that BS 1363 prohibits or restricts using a plug to connect an electricity-generating device to a socket-outlet. Regulation 3 provides that a plug-in microgenerator must comply with the Plug-in Solar Device Interim Product Specification.

conditions: generates electricity from the direct conversion of sunlight into electricity
has a maximum rated alternating current output not exceeding 800 watts
is intended for connection to a low voltage consumer's installation by means of a standard plug and socket
is designed to operate in parallel with a distributor's network

is not designed to import electrical energy from a low voltage consumer's installation for the purpose of storing energy for later supply, other than for control or auxiliary functions permitted by the Plug-in Solar Device Interim Product Specification

battery_storage_excluded.note: Condition (e) of the statutory definition excludes devices designed to import electricity in order to store it for later supply. A plug-in system with a battery that charges from the household supply is therefore not a plug-in microgenerator under this instrument.

product_specification.name: Plug-in Solar Device Interim Product Specification

addresses_dno_notification.note: SI 2026/848 does not mention DNO notification or Engineering Recommendation G98. Notification is a separate framework administered through the Energy Networks Association. The two should not be conflated.

technical_limits.note: Two different caps apply and they are often confused. 800 W is the product cap set by SI 2026/848 for something to count as a plug-in microgenerator. 3.68 kW per phase is the connection-process cap for Engineering Recommendation G98. They serve different purposes.

dno_notification.headline_finding: The 28-day notification deadline is not set by individual network operators. It is a national requirement in EREC G98 section 1.1, made under regulation 22(2)(c) of the Electricity Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations 2002 and the Health and Safety Executive's certificate of exemption of August 2008. EREC G98 places the duty to notify on the installer. SI 2026/848, which makes plug-in solar lawful from 27 August 2026, does not mention EREC G98, DNO notification, or any connection procedure. UK Power Networks, the largest operator by licence area, states on both its installer portal and its consumer guidance that only installers can notify it on behalf of customers. Five of the six operators are consistent with the national 28 days; SP Energy Networks publishes 30 days for its commissioning confirmation form and separately asks for notice before or at commissioning. This is a factual record of what each source states, not legal advice.

national_rule.quote: the Installer is required to ensure that the DNO is made aware of the Micro-generator installation before the time of commissioning or no later than 28 days (inclusive of the day of commissioning) after commissioning
national_rule.source_document: ENA Engineering Recommendation G98, section 1.1 (restated at 8.3.1)
national_rule.legal_basis: Electricity Safety, Quality and Continuity Regulations 2002 Regulation 22(2)(c), and the Certificate of Exemption granted by the Health and Safety Executive in August 2008
national_rule.duty_holder_quote: Your installer must notify the DNO within 28 days of commissioning the generating unit, and provide them with information on the installation. This is a legal requirement.
national_rule.duty_holder_source: ENA Distributed Generation Connection Guide: G98 for Single Premises
national_rule.form: G98 Form B, the Installation Document at Appendix 3 of EREC G98
national_rule.applies_to_diy_householder_note: EREC G98 places the duty on the installer, and still does. No primary source consulted stated what a householder who installs a plug-in device without an installer must do until the Energy Networks Association published a registration portal at https://myplugin.solar/ , read 2026-09-02, whose FAQ states that registering the device there sends the notification to the DNO, and that registration is a legal requirement. That claim is the portal's own; its Terms of Use cite 'the regulations relating to these devices' without naming them. This field stays null because EREC G98 itself is unchanged: it names the installer, not the householder.
national_rule.not_referenced_by_si_2026_848_note: The full text of SI 2026/848 was read on 2026-08-01. It amends product safety requirements and does not mention EREC G98, DNO notification, or any connection procedure. The notification framework is separate from the legalisation.

dno_notification.deadline_uniformity: uniform at 28 days nationally, with SP Energy Networks publishing 30 days for its commissioning confirmation form
dno_notification.headline_finding_note: This field reports what primary sources say. It deliberately draws no conclusion about what a householder installing a plug-in device without an installer is required to do; see national_rule.applies_to_diy_householder, which is null.
